_comment: What proves a directory is DSH Desktop, in one place: the installer (desktop-bridge/install.mjs) and the plugin's status reader (src/browser-electron/bridge-status.ts) both read this file, and a test asserts neither hard-codes a second copy. A generic Electron layout — resources/app/lib/main.js or resources/app.asar — is NOT proof: any Electron app has that shape.

mainEntryCandidates.note: electron-vite layout. The official DSH Desktop 0.14.0 ships this entry with `main: ./out/main/index.js` and no `lib` directory at all (issue #112), while the third-party electron-vite shell (dataelement/dsh-desktop, issue #62) shares the same shape. The `@deepseek-ai/dsh` dependency is what separates them: the official bundle carries it, the third-party shell does not.

_unsupportedNote: Entries listed here are refused with their reason instead of a bare missing-file error. Deliberately empty for out/main/index.js: that IS the official entry (dataelement/dsh-desktop is the official Dataelem desktop, and issue #62 was wrong to call it third-party — its own upstream-baseline.json points at deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). The candidate list above decides by dependency instead.
_layoutNote: resources/app.asar wins over resources/app whenever it exists, so identity is read from the archive in that case and never from the sibling extraction, which the updater leaves behind and which may be a different build.
_tauriNote: DSH Tauri (dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop) runs its own electron-rs main process instead of lib/main.js. Its runtime directory (runtime/<platform>-<arch>) holds electron-rs.json, whose identifier is the proof; the sidebar host patch targets runtime/browser.cjs there by exact sha256 (dsh-host-patch/tauri.json).
_layoutsNote: Where an install keeps its resources and executable. The first layout whose marker exists under the install root applies; the last one has no marker and is the default. A macOS .app bundle keeps resources in Contents/Resources; Windows keeps them in resources/ beside the .exe.
